title: Latent Diffusion
interviewAnswer: Latent diffusion performs the generative process in a compressed latent space rather than pixels, reducing compute while a decoder maps the final latent back to the image domain.
why: Latent diffusion explains how systems such as Stable Diffusion reduce image-generation compute by denoising compressed representations instead of pixels.
intuition: First compress an image into a smaller latent grid with an autoencoder. Run the diffusion process in that latent space, then decode the final latent back to pixels.
deepDive: A pretrained encoder/decoder defines the latent representation. The denoiser operates on lower-resolution/multi-channel latents, reducing spatial compute while retaining semantic content. Conditioning enters via cross-attention/other pathways. The autoencoder is a bottleneck: if it loses details, the diffusion model cannot reconstruct them exactly. Latent scaling/distribution must match training.
workedExample: An image may be encoded from 1024×1024 pixels to a much smaller latent tensor; denoising that tensor is dramatically cheaper than operating on every RGB pixel.
commonMistakes: Saying latent diffusion is just image compression without a generative denoising model.
Ignoring reconstruction limits of the autoencoder.
Mixing latent scales/codecs from incompatible checkpoints.
followUps: Why latent instead of pixel diffusion?
What does the VAE do in Stable Diffusion?
What information can the bottleneck lose?
production: Cache/optimize autoencoder and denoiser separately, version latent codec with the model, and benchmark decode quality plus end-to-end latency.
